<p>BOO on behalf of both Halloween and for<em> poor</em> Coach Saban having to work on his birthday. Not sure he’s getting paid enough to have to work on his bday, right?<span style="color: rgb(31, 73, 125);"> </span>Plus 6 p.m. kick-off for Alabama!? Are you kidding me? That’s prime trick or treating time during <u>our</u> game!? Pretty sure this timing may be attributed to one of the well-documented and highly likely conspiracies below:</p><p>&nbsp;Ohio State used last few weeks not playing to lobby for 6 p.m. Alabama kick-off on Halloween so everyone will be out trick or treating or answering the door for trick or treaters and miss seeing how amazing our team is. Ohio State (starts later) anticipates this schedule line-up will result in sports news/fans wrapped up in Halloween fun only catching the end of <u>their</u> game causing them to speak only of <u>their</u> play and “grand” addition to the season.</p><p>OR</p><p>&nbsp;Mississippi State fans sold their soul for the 6 p.m. kick in hopes everyone would be occupied with Halloween activities and no one would see just how badly Alabama beats them.</p><p>&nbsp;(Based on the information I have read and evidence I have discovered in my own research I am supporting the Ohio State scenario.)</p><p>Poor Alabama parents and fans will have to decide whether to be festive for Halloween or committed to Coach Saban’s process this Saturday. Good luck with your decision, and please do not come trick or treating at my house. While children everywhere are manipulating adults out of their candy, I will be watching Mac Jones and crew taking candy from the baby called the Mississippi State Bull Dawgs. (Chocolate is bad for dogs anyway, and someone needs to tell that to my new little doggie Lola who eats whatever she can find including chipmunks.
